source.title: US and Lebanon protecting wanted Syrian general, BBC finds
source.summary: Bassam al-Hassan, linked to reporter Austin Tice's abduction, is being sheltered in return for information.
source.evidence_text:
A former Syrian general wanted for crimes against humanity , external is being bankrolled and protected by the US and Lebanese authorities, a BBC News investigation has found.
Bassam al-Hassan, who oversaw Syria's chemical weapons programme and was a senior adviser to former President Bashar al-Assad, is being harboured in Lebanon following the Assad regime's collapse in 2024.
An investigation by the BBC and the US broadcaster NPR has discovered that Hassan has been allowed to remain there under an arrangement involving the FBI, and other US and Lebanese authorities. This is because of his willingness to provide information about the abduction of American journalist Austin Tice in Syria in 2012, as well as additional intelligence, we have been told.
Bassam al-Hassan, linked to reporter Austin Tice's abduction, is being sheltered in return for information.
Officials from two different branches of Syria's new government have told the BBC they want Hassan returned to face trial, but that US authorities want him kept in Lebanon, and they say there is little Damascus can do about this.
In response to our findings, Phil Elwood, spokesperson for the Tice family said: "If what you are saying is true, the fact that our tax dollars are being used to furnish a comfortable life for someone associated with the use of chemical weapons on Syrian civilians, who claims to have had Austin Tice executed, is offensive.
Last month the BBC revealed Tice's abduction had been a planned operation , with Hassan in the chain of command.
In it, Hassan is offered "residency", "protection" and help securing his "living needs" in return for information, primarily about Tice.
Yet people connected to the Tice investigation say they have seen little evidence it has significantly advanced since Hassan began providing information as part of this agreement. The deal is believed to have been struck in the spring of 2025.
Sources with knowledge of the investigation have expressed concerns that Hassan's arrangement with the US could continue indefinitely, at significant expense but with little gain.
"This is nothing less than aiding and abetting the escape of a wanted war criminal. The Syrians deserve justice and he should be returned to stand trial."
Sources with knowledge of the arrangement confirmed this was the case, and described to us how Hassan receives money from the US authorities through an intermediary, making it harder to trace. Hassan is sanctioned by the US government.
The businessman, who asked to remain anonymous, said Hassan was valuable, not only because of what he is believed to know about Tice, but because of his knowledge of Syria's chemical weapons programme and its military relationship with Iran - secrets that US intelligence was allegedly interested in.
Hassan told US investigators last year that Tice had been executed on former President Assad's orders, but several people with knowledge of the investigation have questioned the details of his account. Hassan has provided a potential location for Tice's remains, but when the site was searched, nothing was found - according to multiple sources familiar with the dig - casting doubt on the validity of some of Hassan's information.
There are questions, however, over how thoroughly the site was searched. Two sources who said they had intimate knowledge of the operation told the BBC that US authorities stopped digging before the search had been completed, possibly because of security concerns.
Our investigation has found that other Syrian officials connected to the Tice case have also apparently found refuge abroad.

grammar.explanation: We use 'because' to explain why something happens or why someone does something. It connects an action or a situation to its reason.
grammar.example_quote: He is protected because he gives information to the US.

options: Only the US government
The US and Lebanon
Syria's new government

No, Syria's new government wants him to return for a trial.

options: Because he is innocent of crimes.
Because he provides important information.
Because he is a famous general.
option_feedback: The news states he is wanted for crimes, not innocent.
This is correct. He gives information about Austin Tice and other intelligence.

options: The general is wanted, because he is protected.

option_feedback: This does not make sense. He is protected because he gives information, not because he is wanted.
This is correct. The reason Syria's government wants him back is because they want a trial.
While true he disappeared in Syria, 'because' explains the reason for an event, not just where it happened.

They don't know about it.
option_feedback: No, the family expressed that they are upset.

grammar.explanation: The passive voice is used when the focus is on the action and the object receiving the action, rather than the subject performing the action. It is often formed with a form of 'to be' (e.g., is, was, were) followed by the past participle of the main verb. We use it when the performer of the action is unknown, unimportant, or when we want to emphasize the recipient of the action.

lesson.title: US and Lebanon Protect Syrian Officer Linked to Abduction
lesson.overview: A BBC investigation reveals that US and Lebanese authorities are financially supporting and safeguarding a former Syrian officer wanted for crimes, in exchange for intelligence on the disappearance of American journalist Austin Tice.
lesson.topic: International Relations, Espionage, War Crimes, and Human Rights

vocabulary.definition: To provide financial support for someone or something, often in a significant way.
To observe and direct the execution of a task, activity, or group, ensuring it is done correctly.
Organizations, institutions, or groups with a distinct and independent existence.
The action of forcibly taking something or someone, often by legal authority or by force.
To form the basis, support, or foundation for something, strengthening its existence or validity.
The hierarchical arrangement of individuals in positions of authority and decision-making within an organization.
Having few available options or inadequate means to obtain remedy, assistance, or legal redress.
To state a fact or belief confidently and forcefully, often in the face of contradiction.
To be or be considered as; to form or make up a particular part of something.
A person who acts as a link between two parties to facilitate an agreement, communication, or transaction.

grammar.explanation: A participial phrase, often beginning with a present participle (e.g., "leaving," "resulting," "making"), can be used at the end of a sentence to concisely express a result, consequence, or additional information related to the main clause. This construction adds sophistication and flow to writing, allowing for the integration of secondary actions or outcomes without forming a separate clause with a conjunction like "and this leaves" or "which results in."
grammar.example_quote: Officials from Syria's new government seek Hassan's return for trial, but US authorities prefer he remains in Lebanon, leaving Damascus with limited recourse.

quiz.question: What is the primary reason the US and Lebanese authorities are protecting Bassam al-Hassan?
options: To gather intelligence on Syria's current political landscape and military strength.
To secure information about the 2012 disappearance of American journalist Austin Tice and other intelligence.
To facilitate his safe passage to another country following the collapse of the Assad regime.
option_feedback: While Hassan has knowledge of Syria's affairs, the primary stated reason is specifically about Austin Tice and additional intelligence, as detailed in the reading.
The reading explicitly states his willingness to provide intelligence, particularly concerning the seizure of Austin Tice, underpins his protection.
The text indicates he was brought to Lebanon after negotiations, but the protection deal is for ongoing intelligence, not merely safe passage.

quiz.question: According to the Tice family spokesperson, what is the ethical implication of the US supporting Bassam al-Hassan?
options: It demonstrates a regrettable compromise of justice for national security interests.
It is "offensive" and "aiding and abetting the escape of a war criminal."
It suggests a tacit approval of chemical weapons use by the Assad regime.
option_feedback: While this is an inference, the direct quote from the spokesperson is much stronger and more specific in the reading.
The spokesperson explicitly stated it was "offensive" and "aiding and abetting the escape of a war criminal," reflecting their strong condemnation.
The spokesperson linked Hassan to chemical weapons use, but did not directly claim the US was approving such use; their concern was the US supporting Hassan himself.

quiz.question: What role did Bassam al-Hassan previously hold under the Assad regime?
options: He was a key figure in managing Syria's financial institutions and foreign investments.
He was a senior adviser to Bashar al-Assad and supervised the chemical weapons program.
He commanded the forces responsible for internal security and counter-terrorism operations.
option_feedback: The reading does not mention Hassan's involvement in financial institutions.
The text clearly states Hassan "supervised Syria's chemical weapons program and advised former President Bashar al-Assad."
While he was a high-ranking officer, the specific roles mentioned were related to chemical weapons and advising Assad.

quiz.question: How does the practice of Hassan receiving funds via an "intermediary" affect the US authorities?
options: It streamlines the payment process, making it more efficient for US agencies.
It enhances accountability by adding another layer of oversight to financial transactions.
It makes the payments harder to trace, despite Hassan being sanctioned by the US government.
option_feedback: The reading does not suggest efficiency as the purpose of an intermediary for these payments.
An intermediary, in this context, makes tracing harder, which typically reduces transparency and accountability.
The text explicitly states that receiving funds via an "intermediary" makes the payments "harder to track" for the US authorities.

quiz.question: Which of the following best describes the concern raised by individuals involved in the Tice investigation regarding Hassan's deal?
options: The terms of the deal are too lenient, providing Hassan with excessive benefits.
The arrangement might persist for an extended period with minimal tangible progress in the case.
Hassan might be providing disinformation that misleads investigators.
option_feedback: While the Tice family found the comfortable life offensive, the concern from "individuals involved in the Tice investigation" was specifically about the deal continuing "for an unspecified duration with little discernible progress."
The reading states, "individuals involved in the Tice investigation express concerns that Hassan's deal may continue for an unspecified duration with little discernible progress."

Although there are doubts about the validity of some of Hassan's information (like the burial site), the expressed concern about the deal continuing with "little discernible progress" refers to the lack of overall advancement, not necessarily deliberate disinformation.

quiz.question: In the sentence "His willingness to provide intelligence... underpins this arrangement," what does "underpins" most closely mean?
options: Undermines.
Supports.
Overlooks.
option_feedback: "Undermines" means to weaken or subvert, which is the opposite of the meaning in the sentence.
"Underpins" means to support, strengthen, or form the basis of, which aligns with how Hassan's intelligence forms the foundation of his protection.
"Overlooks" means to ignore or miss, which does not fit the context of providing a foundation or basis for an arrangement.

quiz.question: What does the phrase "limited recourse" imply for Damascus regarding Hassan's extradition?
options: The Syrian government has several legal avenues to pursue Hassan's return.
Damascus has few available options or effective means to compel Hassan's return.
International law prevents Damascus from requesting Hassan's extradition from Lebanon.
option_feedback: The text states "leaving Damascus with limited recourse," directly contradicting the idea of "several legal avenues."
"Limited recourse" means having few options or inadequate means to obtain remedy or assistance, which accurately reflects Damascus's inability to force Hassan's return given the US stance.
The reading does not specify international law as the barrier, but rather the US preference for Hassan to remain in Lebanon and Damascus's subsequent lack of leverage.

quiz.question: Consider the sentence: "US authorities prefer he remains in Lebanon, leaving Damascus with limited recourse." If rewritten to emphasize the consequence using a separate clause, which option is correct?
options: US authorities prefer he remains in Lebanon, and this leaves Damascus with limited recourse.
US authorities prefer he remains in Lebanon, because Damascus has limited recourse.
US authorities prefer he remains in Lebanon, although Damascus has limited recourse.
option_feedback: The participial phrase "leaving Damascus with limited recourse" expresses a consequence, and "and this leaves" correctly rephrases this cause-and-effect relationship using a separate clause.
"Because Damascus has limited recourse" suggests that limited recourse is the *reason* for the US preference, which reverses the cause and effect presented in the original sentence.
"Although Damascus has limited recourse" indicates a contrast or concession, which does not accurately convey the direct consequence shown by the participial phrase.

quiz.question: What specifically cast doubt on the "validity" of some of Hassan's information regarding Austin Tice?
options: Hassan's confession that he himself had executed Tice.
The discovery of Tice's remains at a location different from the one Hassan suggested.
The failure to find anything at the potential burial site Hassan provided.
option_feedback: Hassan claimed Tice was executed on Assad's orders, not that he personally executed him.
No remains were found at all, not that they were found elsewhere, which is a key detail.
The reading explicitly states, "when the site was searched, nothing was found - according to multiple sources familiar with the dig - casting doubt on the validity of some of Hassan's information."

quiz.question: What is the Syrian new government's position on Bassam al-Hassan?
options: They support his continued cooperation with US authorities in Lebanon.
They want him returned to face trial for crimes.
They are indifferent to his location as long as he does not return to Syria.
option_feedback: The reading states that "Officials from two different branches of Syria's new government have told the BBC they want Hassan returned to face trial," which contradicts support for his cooperation abroad.
The text clearly states, "Officials from Syria's new government seek Hassan's return for trial."
Their desire for his return to face trial shows they are not indifferent to his location.

quiz.question: Beyond information about Austin Tice, what other intelligence makes Bassam al-Hassan "valuable" to US intelligence?
options: His insights into the internal workings of the new Syrian government.
His knowledge of Syria's chemical weapons program and its military relationship with Iran.

The reading does not mention his knowledge of financial dealings as a reason for his value to US intelligence.

In response to our findings, Phil Elwood, spokesperson for the Tice family said: "If what you are saying is true, the fact that our tax dollars are being used to furnish a comfortable life for someone associated with the use of chemical weapons on Syrian civilians, who claims to have had Austin Tice executed, is offensive.
"This is nothing less than aiding and abetting the escape of a wanted war criminal. The Syrians deserve justice and he should be returned to stand trial."

Sources with knowledge of the arrangement confirmed this was the case, and described to us how Hassan receives money from the US authorities through an intermediary, making it harder to trace. Hassan is sanctioned by the US government.
Sources with knowledge of the investigation have expressed concerns that Hassan's arrangement with the US could continue indefinitely, at significant expense but with little gain.

The businessman, who asked to remain anonymous, said Hassan was valuable, not only because of what he is believed to know about Tice, but because of his knowledge of Syria's chemical weapons programme and its military relationship with Iran - secrets that US intelligence was allegedly interested in.

Hassan told US investigators last year that Tice had been executed on former President Assad's orders, but several people with knowledge of the investigation have questioned the details of his account. Hassan has provided a potential location for Tice's remains, but when the site was searched, nothing was found - according to multiple sources familiar with the dig - casting doubt on the validity of some of Hassan's information.

There are questions, however, over how thoroughly the site was searched. Two sources who said they had intimate knowledge of the operation told the BBC that US authorities stopped digging before the search had been completed, possibly because of security concerns.
Our investigation has found that other Syrian officials connected to the Tice case have also apparently found refuge abroad.
